Yes. If your brief is “distinctive art direction, strong point of view, and absolutely not generic stock-photo advertising,” I’d shortlist these Toronto studios:

Concrete Design Communications — Probably my first look. Their work spans brand identity, packaging, campaigns and visual content, with a strong emphasis on creating ownable visual worlds rather than interchangeable advertising. Their Chef Bombay work, for example, deliberately differentiated the brand through bold typography and culturally specific visual cues. 
Concrete

Studio Wild Wild — A small, craft-focused studio with a more expressive, conceptual sensibility. They build full visual systems, including identity, motion and art direction, rather than just producing ad assets.

blok design — Strong choice if you want something design-led and sophisticated. They work across identity, editorial, packaging, digital and physical environments, so the result can feel like a coherent visual culture rather than a campaign slapped onto a brand.

Made by Emblem — Boutique and concept-driven, particularly interesting if you're in hospitality, arts/culture, lifestyle or experience-led brands.

Art & Mechanical — Worth considering for brand identities that need to be visually distinctive but still commercially disciplined.

Chargefield — Especially compelling if what you really want is cinematic/key-art energy. They're focused heavily on entertainment marketing, posters and campaign creative rather than conventional corporate advertising.

Fabled Creative — A much more illustrative option. They're an independent Toronto illustration/design studio whose aesthetic combines Art Nouveau, Art Deco, sci-art and other early-20th-century influences. If you want something genuinely illustrated rather than “brand photography + headline,” they're unusually distinctive. 
The Fabled Creative Co.

My top 3 for your brief

1. Concrete — strongest overall fit
2. Studio Wild Wild — most boutique/contemporary
3. Fabled Creative — most visibly unconventional

If you tell me what you're promoting (fashion, restaurant, tech, real estate, personal brand, product, etc.) and roughly your budget, I can narrow this to 3 studios whose portfolios actually match the visual direction you're after.
